name: Seven Twenty-Seven
description: Seven Twenty-Seven is an American vying game, often used in dealer's-choice sessions, where players build card totals as close as possible to 7 and 27 while betting between draws.

overview.description: Seven Twenty-Seven is an American vying game, often used in dealer's-choice sessions, where players build card totals as close as possible to 7 and 27 while betting between draws.

history.origins: Seven Twenty-Seven is recorded as an American non-standard poker-style vying game passed through home and dealer's-choice traditions.
timeline: Late 20th century: Circulates in dealer's-choice and home-game contexts.
1999: Rule descriptions appear on major card-game reference sites.
Present: Still played with table-agreed rule variants on over/under handling and declarations.
history.cultural: The game blends poker betting psychology with arithmetic hand-building and variant negotiation before the first deal.
history.evolution: The core frame stayed stable, but house rules differ on whether totals above targets can win, bust, or lose tie-breaks.

setup.deck: 52 cards. Number cards are face value; J/Q/K are 0.5 each; Ace counts as 1 or 11 (and can be interpreted differently for 7 and 27 in the same hand).
setup.dealing: Each player antes. Standard deal: one face-up and one face-down card to each player. Common variation: two face-down and one face-up initially.

rules.objective: Win one or both pot halves by holding the total nearest to 7 and/or nearest to 27 at showdown.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Ante and deal**: Players ante and receive initial cards. 2. **Betting round**: Poker-style pass/bet/call/raise/fold. 3. **Draw decision**: Surviving players may request one extra card or stand pat. 4. **Repeat**: Each draw cycle is followed by another betting round. 5. **Stop condition**: When no player takes another card, showdown occurs. 6. **Showdown split**: Nearest-to-7 winner takes half pot; nearest-to-27 winner takes half pot; ties split their half.
keyRules: Face cards are 0.5 each under standard rules.
Aces are flexible (1 or 11) and can support both targets in evaluation.
If all but one player folds, remaining player wins without showdown.
House rule on above-target totals must be agreed before play.
A perfect 5-A-A can evaluate to both 7 and 27 simultaneously.

strategy.basic: Track both targets simultaneously; a hand that looks weak for 27 may still be live for 7.
strategy.intermediate: Control pot size with marginal dual-purpose hands and pressure opponents who are likely over-extended on one side.
strategy.advanced: Exploit declared or observed house rules on over-target handling; EV swings heavily between 'nearest wins' and 'over is bust'.
tips: Re-evaluate ace value after every draw and bet decision.
Do not chase one side blindly if your hand blocks you from the other half.
Before session start, lock in exact showdown comparison rules.

variations.name: Face-Up Additional Cards
variations.description: Requested extra cards are dealt face up instead of face down.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes card visibility; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Declared Side
variations.description: Players declare 7, 27, or both; declaring both requires sweeping both halves to win anything.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Declaration rules are table-agreed; add overrides when implementation is specified.

variations.name: Over Is Bust
variations.description: Totals above 7 cannot win the 7 side; totals above 27 cannot win anything and may bust immediately.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: House rule changes showdown logic; engine overrides can be added when codified.

scoring.description: Split-pot payout between best 7-side and best 27-side totals among active players at showdown.
scoring.winCondition: Take the whole pot by winning both sides, or half pot by winning one target side.

synthesis.shortDescription: A betting game where each hand can win the 7 side, the 27 side, or both.
